title_seen: Timeloop: A Systematic Approach to DNN Accelerator Evaluation
work_done: Infrastructure that describes accelerator topologies and uses a mapper plus an analytical model to project performance and energy for DNN workloads. Validated against an in-house NVDLA-derived RTL design (detailed simulator) and Eyeriss 65 nm results on 107 DeepBench workloads.
advantages: Covers a broad architecture and mapping space with one representation. Energy within 8% of the NVDLA-derived baseline for all 107 workloads; cycle accuracy 78-99%, mean 95%.
disadvantages: Throughput-based model assumes minimal fill/drain disruption; six outlier workloads at 78-88% due to stalls from hardware data layout. Reference is a detailed simulator of an RTL design, not FPGA/board counters.
relevance: Main ASIC-oriented analytical model to contrast with V3's exact (0-cycle) model = RTL = board agreement; its error sources (fill/drain, stalls) are what V3 models explicitly.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. VII A-C (validation), Figs. 8-10
notes: Validation reported: NVDLA-derived reference energy within 8%, cycles 78-99% (mean 95%); Eyeriss comparison recreates published Fig. 10.

title_seen: Understanding Reuse, Performance, and Hardware Cost of DNN Dataflows: A Data-Centric Approach Using MAESTRO
work_done: Defines data-centric directives for DNN dataflows and an analytical cost model (MAESTRO) for runtime, energy and reuse; drives a DSE over 480M designs. Runtime validated against MAERI RTL simulation (VGG16, 64 PEs) and Eyeriss reported AlexNet runtime.
advantages: Runtime within 3.9% absolute error on average vs cycle-accurate RTL and reported delay; 1029-4116x faster than the equivalent RTL simulation; compiler-friendly dataflow notation.
disadvantages: Error is nonzero and averaged over CONV layers of two designs; Eyeriss comparison uses paper-reported runtime, not measured hardware. Sparsity modelled only as uniform distribution.
relevance: Per-layer dataflow cost model of the kind a V3 compiler could use for mode selection; contrast with V3's exact per-layer cycle model.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 1, Sec. 4.4-4.5 (Model Validation), Fig. 9
notes: arXiv v6 title says 'Dataflows ... Using MAESTRO'; Crossref title 'Understanding Reuse, Performance, and Hardware Cost of DNN Dataflow' (truncated). Intro: '90-95% accuracy of actual open-source RTL'.

title_seen: A Systematic Methodology for Characterizing Scalability of DNN Accelerators using SCALE-Sim
work_done: Presents SCALE-Sim, a cycle-accurate systolic-array DNN simulator (SRAM/DRAM traces, runtime, bandwidth), plus an analytical runtime model used to study scale-up vs scale-out. Validated against an RTL systolic array (OS dataflow) for matmuls at varying array sizes.
advantages: Directly models systolic OS/WS/IS arrays with cycle-level traces; RTL and simulator cycle counts shown 'in good agreement' (Fig. 4); analytical model prunes search space quickly.
disadvantages: Validation uses only matrix multiplications under full utilization, shown graphically with no error figure; analytical model ignores memory-limited bandwidth effects; no FPGA or silicon measurement.
relevance: Closest modelled architecture to V3 (systolic OS array); V3 extends model-RTL agreement to whole CNN layers and the board.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. II-D (Validation of the tool), Fig. 4, Sec. III intro
notes: Peer-reviewed version of SCALE-Sim (ISPASS 2020). arXiv 1811.02883 (v1 tool paper, not peer-reviewed) has the same validation text. SCALE-Sim v3 (ISPASS 2025, DOI 10.1109/ISPASS64960.2025.00026) is a spare; Crossref API did not return JSON for it during this check.

title_seen: Performance Modeling for CNN Inference Accelerators on FPGA
work_done: Analytical performance and resource model for a loop-unrolled/tiled FPGA CNN accelerator, used for early DSE. Throughput and latency validated against on-board tests on Arria 10 and Stratix 10 with different MAC counts, 16-bit fixed point.
advantages: Board-validated: estimate vs on-board results within 3%; replaces 6-8 h Quartus compilations in DSE; models external and on-chip memory accesses.
disadvantages: Residual error attributed to DRAM transfer latency mismatch, minor layers (e.g., average pooling) and pipeline stages; validated for one design strategy on Intel FPGAs, power not modelled.
relevance: FPGA analytical model validated on boards with few-% error; V3 claims exact agreement and removes the cited error sources.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. I contributions, Sec. VIII-C (Performance Model Validation), Fig. 14
notes: Author accepted/published version on NSF PAR. The 'within 3%' figure is now confirmed from the text (was secondary in t4).

title_seen: DNNExplorer: A Framework for Modeling and Exploring a Novel Paradigm of FPGA-based DNN Accelerator
work_done: FPGA accelerator paradigm mixing a layer-wise pipeline and a generic reusable structure, with analytical performance/resource models and a DSE engine. Pipeline model checked against board results on ZC706 and KU115; generic-structure model against 36 CONV cases on VU9P.
advantages: Board-level validation: 1.15% average error (pipeline model, 6 and 8 DNNs) and 2.17% average error (generic structure, 36 CONV layers); up to 4.2x over DNNBuilder for a 38-layer VGG-like net.
disadvantages: Errors are averages, not per-cycle exact; generic-structure validation uses single CONV layers; evaluation on Xilinx devices other than Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC KV260.
relevance: FPGA DSE model with board-validated error and DPU comparison; V3 contrasts its 0-cycle model and also uses the DPU as baseline.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 6.1-6.2 (Accelerator Modeling), Figs. 7-8
notes: The 1.15%/2.17% figures previously attributed to DNNBuilder (secondary) are reported here in DNNExplorer's own text. Crossref title is 'DNNExplorer' only.

title_seen: Optimizing FPGA-based Accelerator Design for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
work_done: Roofline-based analytical DSE of loop tiling/unrolling for an HLS CNN accelerator, computing compute roof and computation-to-communication ratio per design; implemented on a VC707 (Virtex-7 485T) at 100 MHz, 61.62 GFLOPS peak.
advantages: Classic method linking tile/unroll choices to compute and bandwidth bounds; per-layer execution-cycle estimates (Table 4) drive a cross-layer uniform unroll choice; board timing reported per layer (Table 7).
disadvantages: 32-bit float AlexNet CONV layers only; in the sections read no explicit model-vs-board error figure is reported; HLS pre-synthesis reports used for estimation.
relevance: Key classic for analytical FPGA CNN DSE; V3 uses a cycle model rather than a roofline bound.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 3.4-3.5 (DSE, Table 4), Sec. 5 (Tables 5-8)
notes: Copy hosted on a Cambridge course reading list. Validation statement limited to: model used to select design, board performance measured; no estimate-vs-measured error found by grep for estimat/measur/error.

title_seen: AutoDNNchip: An Automated DNN Chip Predictor and Builder for Both FPGAs and ASICs
work_done: Chip Predictor (graph-based accelerator model for energy, throughput, latency, area) and Chip Builder (DSE plus RTL generation) for FPGA and ASIC. Predictor validated against measurements on Ultra96 FPGA, edge TPU and Jetson TX2 (15 DNNs) and Eyeriss/ShiDianNao reported data.
advantages: Measured-hardware validation across platforms: latency error 1.78-5.98% (avg 3.73%) on Ultra96, max 9.75% overall; energy max 9.17%; generated designs up to 3.86x over expert designs.
disadvantages: Errors up to ~10%; larger errors where operations are unsupported (edge TPU) or strides >2 (Eyeriss); unit parameters must be measured or synthesized per platform.
relevance: Board-validated predictor on a Zynq UltraScale+ (Ultra96) edge FPGA, the same family as KV260; contrast with V3 exactness.
read_locator: full text: abstract, subsection Validation of the Chip Predictor, Figs. 8-10, Table 7

title_seen: ZigZag: A Memory-Centric Rapid DNN Accelerator Design Space Exploration Framework
work_done: Memory-centric DSE framework with a latency-enhanced analytical cost estimator, temporal mapping generator supporting uneven mapping, and architecture generator. Validated against Eyeriss/ENVISION reported energy, an in-house accelerator's post-synthesis RTL data, and Timeloop+Accelergy/Interstellar.
advantages: Energy within 5% / 7.5% of Eyeriss / ENVISION reported values; vs in-house RTL max 6% energy and 9% PE utilisation error; uneven mapping finds up to 33% more energy-efficient points.
disadvantages: Validation is mostly energy and utilisation, against reported chip values and post-synthesis data rather than measured cycle counts; ASIC-oriented, no FPGA board evaluation.
relevance: Analytical DSE with RTL-referenced validation; contrast for V3's exact cycle agreement.
read_locator: full text (arXiv v3): abstract, Sec. VI Validation, Figs. 14-16
notes: arXiv title differs from the published TC title 'ZigZag: Enlarging Joint Architecture-Mapping Design Space Exploration for DNN Accelerators'; arXiv v3 read, published version may differ.

title_seen: Accelergy: An Architecture-Level Energy Estimation Methodology for Accelerator Designs
work_done: Architecture-level energy estimation methodology with user-defined compound and primitive components and plug-in estimators; validated on an Eyeriss design written in RTL and placed-and-routed in 65 nm, using AlexNet weights and ImageNet inputs (16-bit).
advantages: Total energy within 5% of post-layout results and relative breakdown within 8%; captures action-dependent energy; companion to Timeloop.
disadvantages: Energy only (no latency/cycle model); single validation design (Eyeriss, 65 nm ASIC); ground truth is post-layout simulation, not silicon or FPGA measurement.
relevance: Energy-model counterpart; V3 measures energy on the board (INA260) rather than estimating it.
read_locator: full text: abstract, Sec. 5.1 setup, Sec. 5.3 Energy Estimation Validation, Fig. 6
